results.title: World Cup: Emerse Fae believes Ivory Coast can compete vs Germany | Flashscore.com
highlights:
# EXCLUSIVE: Ivory Coast’s Fae fires warning to Germany and reveals selection headache
[...]
Head coach Emerse Fae has expressed confidence that Ivory Coast national can compete strongly against Germany at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
[...]
Speaking to Flashscore, Fae insisted the African champions will not sit back against Germans, stressing that his players will approach the match with confidence and belief rather than fear.
[...]
"As for our approach, I don’t want the team to sit back and play too cautiously," said the 42-year-old.
[...]
"That’s not my philosophy. I’m not afraid of any opponent, including Germany. I want us to play with confidence, go forward, and try to score goals rather than just defend and rely on counter-attacks."
[...]
Reflecting on the matches, Fae explained that the main objective was to find the right balance between defence and attack.
[...]
He also admitted that selecting the final squad will be a difficult task, as many players have stepped up and shown they deserve a place.
[...]
"The key lesson from the two matches is that we can be strong both defensively and in attack," he continued.
[...]
"So, our aim in these games was to strike a balance, being just as strong defensively as we are going forward, and we’ve achieved that.
[...]
"A lot depends on the team spirit, and once again, it was very good. Winning these two matches boosts confidence, but it also makes selection difficult, as many players have shown they deserve a place in the 26-man World Cup squad."
[...]
"After the AFCON, I felt we were scoring plenty of goals but also conceding too many. So, it was crucial for us to improve defensively, and I’m very pleased with how the team has responded.
[...]
"We have many players who deserve to be there (at the World Cup), but we can only select 26. That makes it a tough decision for the technical team.
[...]
Coach Fae has defended his continued reliance on Franck Kessie, insisting the midfielder’s experience remains crucial to Ivory Coast.
[...]
The former Nice and Nantes star has made it clear that Kessie’s value goes far beyond physical attributes stating that the Al Ahli midfielder remains a central figure in the squad, not only as captain but also as a leader.
[...]
When asked about his target at the global showpiece, he said: "I have believed for some time now, especially after what we saw in Ivory Coast (AFCON 2023) that African teams need to have more belief in themselves because they have the quality to achieve something great.
[...]
"I believe Ivory Coast has the potential to do something special. We will go into the tournament with the aim of winning every game, taking it one match at a time, and pushing as far as possible. Why not aim for the final?"

results.title: Ivory Coast World Cup 2026 Guide: Squad, Key Players & Group E Preview | Fanorate
highlights:
Ivory Coast at World Cup 2026: AFCON champions return. Squad, Emerse Faé’s tactics, Amad Diallo, key players and full Group E guide from Fanorate.
[...]
Head Coach Emerse Faé Led Ivory Coast to the 2023 AFCON title after taking over mid-tournament
[...]
The current side carries a fresh kind of momentum. Ivory Coast won the 2023 Africa Cup of Nations on home soil in dramatic fashion, and that triumph is tied to a remarkable story: Emerse Faé took over as coach mid-tournament and guided the team to the title — reportedly the first manager ever appointed during an international tournament to go on and win it. That belief carries into 2026.
[...]
There is also the Faé narrative: a young, homegrown coach who pulled off one of football’s great in-tournament rescues now leading his country at a World Cup. Add a squad blending Premier League names like Manchester United’s Amad Diallo with experienced European-based stars, and the Elephants are a compelling watch — gifted,
[...]
, and finally drawn into a group they can
[...]
For the first time in their history, Ivory Coast have a genuinely favorable World Cup draw. Germany are the clear group favorites, but the battle for the second qualifying spot is wide open between the Elephants and Ecuador, with Curaçao the clear outsiders.
[...]
Under Faé, Ivory Coast favor an athletic, aggressive style built on physical midfield dominance and quick attacking transitions. Expect a 4-3-3 or 4-2-3-1 with Sangaré shielding the defense, Kessié driving forward, and pace on the wings through Diallo and others. The Elephants press energetically and look to win the ball high, then attack at speed. Their strength is athleticism and individual quality in wide areas; the historical weakness has been game management and finishing in tight matches.
[...]
Ivory Coast have appeared at three previous World Cups — 2006, 2010 and 2014 — and have never advanced past the group stage. Their misfortune was being drawn into brutal groups during the Drogba era. In 2006 they faced Argentina and the Netherlands. In 2010 they were grouped with Brazil and Portugal, beating North Korea 3–0 but going out on goal difference. In 2014 a late penalty against Greece ended their hopes. The 2026 tournament, with its kinder draw and 48-team format, represents their best-ever chance to finally reach the knockout rounds — buoyed by their 2023 AFCON triumph.
[...]
Ivory Coast to battle Ecuador for second place in Group E. We project them to advance for the first time in their history — likely as runners-up to Germany — and reach the round of 32, with the round of 16 a realistic next step. This is the year the group-stage curse finally ends.

Following the 2023 AFCON, where a 4-0 loss to Equatorial Guinea led to an early group-stage exit and the departure of Jean-Louis Gasset, Emerse Fae took the reins. Dubbed the "miracle manager," Fae transitioned from assistant to permanent head coach after orchestrating an incredible turnaround for the national team. Under his guidance, the squad eliminated defending champions Senegal, overcame Mali while playing with ten men, and ultimately defeated Nigeria in the final to secure the title in front of a home crowd.
[...]
In addition to this continental success, Fae became the first locally appointed Ivorian manager to lead the Elephants through a successful World Cup qualification campaign.
[...]
Emerse Faé’s tactical approach: Faé favours a compact 4-3-3 with quick transitions, Seko Fofana pushing forward from midfield, and wide threats such as Amad Diallo, Simon Adingra, and Yan Diomande. For the World Cup, Evann Guessand leads the line after Sébastien Haller was named among the standby players.
[...]
Emerse Fae aims to guide the Elephants to their first-ever knockout stage at the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Emphasizing a professional mindset for the tournament in the United States, Fae believes advancing from their group is an attainable objective.
[...]
The Ivory Coast enters the World Cup as a potent and youthful wild card, having been placed in a group with South American competitors Ecuador, debutants Curacao, and European titans Germany. The Elephants will attempt to progress beyond the group stage for the first time in their history by combining defensive solidity with an aggressive offensive approach.
